toc.title: Where AI fits, techniques and the AWS AI services
Choosing between approaches, the service chooser and practice

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. AI: artificial intelligence; ML: machine learning; NLP: natural language processing

  • Recognize where AI and ML add value, and where they are not appropriate
  • Pick the right technique: classification, regression or clustering
  • Give real-world examples of AI applications
  • Explain what Transcribe, Translate, Comprehend, Lex, Polly, Rekognition, Textract, Personalize and SageMaker AI do
  • Decide when a traditional ML model or a foundation model fits

2Where AI fits, techniques and the AWS AI services

Running case

Cedar and Salt's AI Wish List

  • The leaders list six wishes: turn call recordings into text, translate listings, find review sentiment, read scanned invoices, recommend trips, and build a booking chatbot
  • A seventh wish is a fixed 15 percent group discount
  • Some wishes need AI; one does not
  • Your job: match each wish to the right technique or AWS service, and spot the one that needs plain code

Where AI and ML Add Value

  • Assist human decision making: rank risky bookings so a person reviews the top few
  • Scale a solution: answer thousands of traveler questions at the same time
  • Automate repetitive work: tag photos, route emails and extract data from forms
  • Find patterns people cannot see in large amounts of data
  • AI usually supports people; it does not replace every decision
Exam tip

Assist, scale and automate are the three classic reasons to use AI.

When AI Is Not Appropriate

  • A specific outcome is needed, not a prediction: use a rule or formula, such as a fixed discount
  • The cost-benefit does not work: data, build and run costs exceed the value
  • There is too little data, or it is poor quality
  • Errors are costly and nobody can review them
  • A simpler solution already does the job
Exam tip

If the answer is known and exact, write code instead of training a model.

Matching the Technique to the Problem

Technique What it predicts or finds Example at Cedar and Salt
Classification A category Will this booking be canceled: yes or no?
Regression A number What nightly price will fill the room?
Clustering Groups in unlabeled data Which guest segments exist?
  • Classification and regression use labeled data (supervised); clustering uses unlabeled data
Exam tip

Category: classification. Number: regression. Groups: clustering.

Real-World AI Applications

Application Example at Cedar and Salt
Computer vision Checking listing photos for unsafe content
NLP Summarizing and classifying reviews
Speech recognition Transcribing support calls
Recommendation systems "Trips you may like"
Fraud detection Flagging suspicious payments
Forecasting Predicting demand by season
Knowledge bases Answering policy questions from company documents
Agentic AI A booking agent that plans and acts
Exam tip

Match the task to the field: see, read, listen, recommend, flag, predict, look up or act.

Ready-Made Services, SageMaker AI or Foundation Models

  • Ready-made AI services: call an application programming interface (API); no ML expertise needed (this module)
  • Amazon SageMaker AI: build, train and deploy your own models (Module 3)
  • Foundation models through Amazon Bedrock: generative AI (Modules 4 to 7)
  • Moving down the list gives more control and takes more effort

Exam tip

A common task with no ML skills in the team: start with a ready-made AI service.

Speech and Language: Transcribe, Translate and Polly

Service What it does Think
Amazon Transcribe Automatic speech recognition: converts audio to text, in real time or from files in S3 Speech to text
Amazon Translate Text translation between languages, on demand Language to language
Amazon Polly Converts text into lifelike speech with generative, neural and standard voices Text to speech
  • Chain them: Transcribe, then Translate, then Polly gives spoken translation
Exam tip

Audio in: Transcribe. Text in another language: Translate. Speech out: Polly.

Text and Documents: Comprehend and Textract

Service What it does Think
Amazon Comprehend NLP insights from text: entities, key phrases, language, sentiment, personally identifiable information (PII) and topics; custom classification Meaning in text
Amazon Textract Extracts printed and handwritten text, forms and tables from scanned documents and PDFs, with queries, invoices and receipts and ID analysis Data out of documents
  • Comprehend understands text that is already text; Textract reads the scanned page first
Exam tip

Sentiment or entities: Comprehend. Fields and tables from a scan: Textract.

Images and Video: Amazon Rekognition

  • Amazon Rekognition is a deep learning image and video analysis service
  • It detects objects, scenes and text, and unsafe content for moderation
  • It analyzes and compares faces, including face liveness checks
  • Custom Labels train a classifier for your own objects, such as logos
  • It needs no ML expertise; call the API on files in Amazon S3
Exam tip

Objects, faces and unsafe content in pictures or video: Rekognition.

Conversation and Recommendations: Lex and Personalize

Service What it does Think
Amazon Lex Builds conversational interfaces for voice and text with speech recognition and natural language understanding Chatbots
Amazon Personalize Fully managed service that makes item recommendations and user segments from your interaction data Recommendations
  • Lex works with AWS Lambda to carry out the request
  • Personalize learns from clicks and purchases, not from the content of items
Exam tip

A chatbot with voice or text: Lex. "People like you also booked": Personalize.

Amazon SageMaker AI: Your Own Models Old name [Dates]

  • Amazon SageMaker AI is a fully managed ML service
  • Data scientists and developers build, train and deploy ML models in a hosted environment
  • It supports built-in algorithms, your own algorithms and frameworks, and foundation models
  • Use it when no ready-made service fits, such as a custom fraud model
  • On 3 December 2024 Amazon SageMaker was renamed SageMaker AI Old name
Exam tip

Ready-made task: an AI service. Your own data and model: SageMaker AI.

3Choosing between approaches, the service chooser and practice

Traditional ML or a Foundation Model?

Situation Better fit
Structured, tabular prediction such as cancellation or price Traditional ML
Regulatory concerns: regulators need an explanation of each decision Traditional ML: more explainable
Very high volume with tight cost, latency and operational limits Traditional ML: smaller models
Generate, summarize or translate free text; open-ended chat Foundation model
Many different language tasks, little labeled data Foundation model: just prompt it
Exam tip

Explainable and structured: traditional ML. Open-ended language or content: a foundation model.

Service Chooser: I Need To...

I need to... Use
Turn call recordings into text Amazon Transcribe
Translate listings into other languages Amazon Translate
Find the sentiment and entities in reviews Amazon Comprehend
Pull fields and tables from scanned invoices Amazon Textract
Flag unsafe content in photos Amazon Rekognition
Read text out loud Amazon Polly
Build a voice or text chatbot Amazon Lex
Recommend trips to each traveler Amazon Personalize
Train my own model Amazon SageMaker AI
Exam tip

Name the verb in the need, then the service.

What the Exam Asks: Use Cases and Services

  • Where it helps: assist decisions, scale, automate
  • Where it does not: exact rules, poor cost-benefit, little data, costly errors
  • Which technique: classification, regression or clustering
  • Which service: Transcribe, Translate, Comprehend, Textract, Rekognition, Polly, Lex, Personalize or SageMaker AI
  • Which model type: traditional ML for explainable, structured tasks; a foundation model for open-ended language
Exam tip

Read the verb in the question, then pick the service or technique.

Design Check: Cedar and Salt's Wish List

Wish Choose
Call recordings into text Amazon Transcribe
Listings in many languages Amazon Translate
Review sentiment Amazon Comprehend
Scanned invoices into fields Amazon Textract
Trip recommendations Amazon Personalize
A booking chatbot Amazon Lex
A fixed 15 percent group discount Plain code, not AI
A custom fraud model on its own data Amazon SageMaker AI
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Cedar and Salt wants to turn recordings of customer support calls into text. Which AWS service should it use?

  • AAmazon Polly, which converts text into speech
  • BAmazon Transcribe, which converts audio into text
  • CAmazon Translate, which translates text between languages
  • DAmazon Comprehend, which finds sentiment and entities in text
Show the answer

Answer: B. Amazon Transcribe is an automatic speech recognition service that converts audio to text. Polly does the reverse, Translate changes the language of text, and Comprehend analyzes text that already exists.

S2The finance team receives scanned supplier invoices and wants the invoice numbers, dates and line-item tables as structured data. Which service fits best?

  • AAmazon Textract, which extracts text, forms and tables from documents
  • BAmazon Rekognition, which detects objects, people and faces in images and videos
  • CAmazon Polly, which turns written text into lifelike spoken speech in many voices
  • DAmazon Lex, which builds conversational chatbots for voice and text channels
Show the answer

Answer: A. Textract extracts printed and handwritten text, forms and tables from scanned documents, and it has an operation for invoices and receipts. Rekognition analyzes pictures, Polly makes speech, and Lex builds chatbots.

S3Which TWO of these are classification problems? (Select TWO.)

  • APredicting whether a booking will be canceled
  • BEstimating next month's revenue as a number
  • CGrouping guests into segments without labels
  • DFlagging a payment as fraudulent or legitimate
  • EPredicting the best nightly price in dollars
Show the answer

Answer: A, D. Classification predicts a category, such as canceled or not, and fraudulent or legitimate. Estimating revenue or a price is regression because it predicts a number, and grouping without labels is clustering.

S4Cedar and Salt's policy says every booking of ten or more guests gets exactly 15 percent off. How should the team implement it?

  • ATrain a regression model on past discounts
  • BUse a foundation model to guess the discount
  • CCluster past bookings to find the discount
  • DUse plain code, because the outcome is exact
Show the answer

Answer: D. When a specific outcome is required instead of a prediction, a rule or formula is the right tool. A model could produce a wrong discount, and the cost of building and running one is not justified.

S5Cedar and Salt wants to show each traveler trips they are likely to book, based on what they and similar travelers clicked and booked. Which service is built for this?

  • AAmazon Comprehend
  • BAmazon Rekognition
  • CAmazon Personalize
  • DAmazon Translate
Show the answer

Answer: C. Personalize is a fully managed service that generates item recommendations from interaction data such as clicks and purchases. Comprehend analyzes text, Rekognition analyzes images and video, and Translate translates text.

S6The team wants a booking chatbot that understands typed and spoken requests and walks the traveler through a conversation. Which service should it use?

  • AAmazon Textract
  • BAmazon Lex
  • CAmazon Polly
  • DAmazon Transcribe
Show the answer

Answer: B. Amazon Lex builds conversational interfaces for voice and text with speech recognition and natural language understanding. Polly only speaks, Transcribe only converts speech to text, and Textract reads documents.

S7A lender must explain every credit decision to regulators, and its data is a structured table of customer attributes. Which approach fits best?

  • AA large foundation model that generates a free-text decision
  • BA chatbot built with a conversational service
  • CA model for recognizing faces in photos
  • DA traditional ML model, which is easier to explain
Show the answer

Answer: D. Structured data and a regulatory need for explanations point to a traditional ML model. Foundation models are better for open-ended language and content, and the other options solve unrelated tasks.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Value assist decisions, scale and automate
Not appropriate an exact outcome, poor cost-benefit, little data, costly errors
Techniques classification for categories, regression for numbers, clustering for groups
Services Transcribe, Translate, Polly, Comprehend, Textract, Rekognition, Lex, Personalize, SageMaker AI
Which model traditional ML for explainable structured tasks, a foundation model for open-ended language
